question: The community workshop had 213 sheets of plywood in its rack. A stage-building job used 64 of them over the winter. A timber merchant delivered 67 sheets in February, and a closing factory donated 44 more. The workshop is open 5 days a week. Every sheet in the rack was cut into 4 shelf boards for the housing project. Damp in the store warped 75 of the boards and they were rejected. How many shelf boards were usable?

Bruno came back from the coast with 25 boxes of shells, and each box held 8 shells. His sister Carla, who had filled far more boxes than he had, gave him 79 shells from her own collection. He found 15 of his shells broken when he unpacked them and threw those away. A second trip added 71 shells to the tray. The walk to the beach takes 40 minutes. Every shell in the tray was threaded onto a cord with 3 wooden beads. How many wooden beads did Bruno use?

The roastery opened the morning with 193 sacks of coffee, and every sack is split into 8 retail bags. A dozen baristas came in for the training session. The sample room sent up 9 extra bags, and the roasting floor added 9 more that had been held back for testing. The company weighs its coffee in grams rather than in kilograms. In the evening the manager worked out that each bag brews 4 full pots. How many pots of coffee would the stock brew?

The museum has 221 display cases, and every case holds 8 exhibits. The curator Leah brought up 68 further exhibits from the basement store, rather more than her colleague Tom had managed to find. Each exhibit on show was photographed 3 times for the new catalogue. The picture editor rejected 4598 of those photographs as too dark to print. How many photographs were kept for the catalogue?

A fruit wholesaler unloaded 176 boxes of apples at the depot, and every box held 7 apples. Sorting found 73 apples bruised, and those went to the cider press instead. A late crate added 10 more apples to the pile. The kitchen then cut every apple in the pile into 3 slices for the school lunches, so the count tripled. How many apple slices went to the schools?

Mira printed 55 large sheets for the fairground, and each sheet was perforated into 4 ride tickets. She and her colleague Sten divided the tickets equally among the 4 stalls, and Mira kept the batch for the gate stall while Sten took the rest. Every ticket in her batch is good for 7 rides on the carousel. Over the weekend riders used up 235 of those rides. Each ride still unused is worth 3 loyalty points, and the fair added 45 bonus points to Mira's card. How many loyalty points did Mira have?

The bakery opened the morning with 99 trays, and each tray carried 9 bread rolls, with all baking times written in minutes rather than in hours. Before noon 472 rolls were sold at the counter. A second bake added 21 rolls to the racks. During the afternoon the rolls were shared equally among the 5 shops in the group, and the driver stayed with the delivery for the Elm Street shop. In the evening that shop sold 21 rolls to a restaurant. How many rolls did the Elm Street shop have left?

The brickworks had 214 pallets in the yard when the gates opened, and each pallet was stacked with 8 boxes. Every box on those pallets holds 7 bricks. Half of the yard is under cover. A storeman found 32 loose bricks by the kiln and added them to the tally. During the afternoon 7828 bricks went out to the housing site. In the evening every brick still in the yard was split cleanly in two for the decorative wall, giving twice as many pieces. How many pieces were in the yard?

Kemal cut 173 lengths of leather at his bench, and each length yields 5 straps. His colleague Deniz, whose output was smaller that week, handed over 21 finished straps. Half of the straps are dyed black. The bag orders used up 695 straps before the end of the month. Kemal found 13 straps among his offcuts and bought 31 more from a tannery. Every strap still on the rack needs 3 rivets before it can be sold. How many rivets does the rack need?

The dairy depot counted 222 crates of milk in the chill room in the morning, and it prints its volumes in millilitres rather than in litres. The first round delivered 175 crates to the shops. The dairy sent up 60 fresh crates, a cafe returned 11 empties that were counted back in, and the second run brought back 70 crates. A dozen drivers work out of the yard. During the afternoon the crates were shared equally among the 4 village shops, and the supervisor followed the load for Ashby. In the evening 68 further crates were delivered to Ashby. How many crates did the Ashby shop have?

Rui counted 240 empty bottles at the recycling point when he arrived in the morning. His colleague Sara, whose van had collected more than his that week, unloaded 25 bottles, and a cafe left 28 by the gate. Each bottle handed in is worth 4 deposit tokens. During the afternoon 691 tokens were redeemed by people at the kiosk. In the evening a school collection brought in 72 more tokens, and a walker handed over 8 tokens he had found. How many tokens did the recycling point hold?

The gym issued 210 day passes in the first week of January, and a promotion doubled the number issued so twice as many were in circulation. Ana, the manager, gave out 39 more to staff, rather more than her deputy Bram had handed out. The pool is 25 metres long, and sessions there are booked in minutes rather than in hours. An audit found 90 of the passes had expired and cancelled them. Every valid pass entitles its holder to 5 visits, and members have already used 519 visits. How many visits are still available?

The village cafe had 31 cakes on its stand at opening, and the baker brought out 30 more during the morning. Every cake was cut in half for the tasting event, so the number of pieces doubled. The pieces were then shared equally between the 2 serving counters, and the owner kept an eye only on the window counter. The kitchen sent out 40 more pieces to that counter later on. How many pieces were on the window counter?

The garden pond started the spring with 15 water lilies. The gardener lifted out 8 of them because they had crowded the edge. Every lily left in the water sent out 5 new shoots by June. The gardener planted 37 further shoots from a nursery tray and was given 20 more by a neighbour. The pond measures 9 metres across at its widest. Each shoot opened 2 flowers that summer, twice what the older plants had managed. How many flowers opened on the pond?

The cable factory had 165 drums in its store and took in 77 more from the drawing shop. Every drum carries 8 coils of copper cable. Each coil was cut in half for the transport contract, so the number of pieces doubled. The factory runs 3 shifts a day. A technician added 9 spare pieces from the test rig to the batch. Every piece needs 6 connectors before it can be installed, and the contract used up 21233 connectors. How many connectors were left in the store?

Amir had 114 blank keycards for the new building, and the system logs access times in minutes rather than in hours. His colleague Ruth, who had ordered more than he had, gave him 68 cards from her own box. Testing showed 31 of the cards to be faulty and they were destroyed. Every working card is programmed to open 9 doors in the complex. The security review then revoked 26 of those door permissions. How many door permissions were active?

The stationer had 39 boxes of chalk on the shelf at the start of term, and the shop has been trading for 11 years. A local school bought 35 of the boxes in one order. A wholesaler then delivered 76 boxes, and a closing college donated 21 more. Half of the chalk in stock is white. Over the term 87 boxes were sold across the counter. The remaining boxes were divided equally between 2 classrooms, and the caretaker carried one classroom's share upstairs. How many boxes went upstairs?

The school planted 33 tomato plants in its polytunnel in the spring. A cold snap in May killed 15 of them before they flowered. Every plant that survived carried 6 trusses by the middle of the summer. Each truss ripened 5 tomatoes for the cookery lessons. The gardening club saved 5 seeds from every tomato for the following year. How many seeds did the club save?

On Saturday morning Maya counted 159 seashells in her collection box. Before lunch she sold 97 of them at the beach market. In the afternoon she split what was left into 2 equal piles, kept half of them in the box and gave the other pile to her cousin. Her friend Ravi keeps his own shells in a tin, and all day his tin held fewer shells than Maya's box. That evening Maya picked up 14 more shells on the sand and dropped them into her box. Just before bed she handed 28 shells from the box to her little brother. How many seashells are in Maya's box now?

Nadia runs a school bookshop. She began the term with 198 packs of pencils on her shelf. A large delivery made the number of packs on that shelf 2 times what it had been. Each pack holds 7 pencils, and she emptied every pack into one big bin. Over the term students bought 2271 pencils from the bin, and her colleague Tomas, who sold fewer pencils than Nadia did, took 6 pencils out of it for the art room. How many pencils are left in the bin?

A market stall keeps its takings in a coin tin, counting everything in cents and turning the cents into dollars only at closing time. At the start of Saturday morning the tin held 211 cents. A customer added 7 cents in change during the first hour, and then 209 cents were taken out to pay a delivery boy. Around midday a passer-by dropped 27 cents into the tin, and in the early afternoon a sale brought in 46 cents. In the evening the stallholder removed 41 cents to buy a bread roll. How many cents are in the tin at the end of the day?

A dairy records all of its volumes in millilitres, although the labels it prints show litres. On Monday each of the dairy's 6 vans was loaded with 217 crates of milk, and every crate holds 7 bottles. That morning 3402 bottles were sold at the market. A shop returned 65 unopened bottles to the vans in the afternoon. Later 3941 bottles were dropped off at schools along the route. How many bottles are still on the vans?

Farmer Otto packs his eggs into boxes. On Monday there were 226 boxes in each of his 4 barns. That afternoon he sent 592 boxes to a supermarket. Every box that stayed on the farm holds 6 trays, each tray holds 2 rows, and each row holds 7 eggs. His neighbour Petra keeps fewer boxes on her farm than Otto keeps on his. How many eggs are still on Otto's farm?

Nina sold 49 raffle tickets at 5 dollars each on the first day of the school fair. A local shop then added a 67 dollar donation to that day's takings. Each of the 4 days of the fair brought in exactly the same amount as the first day, so the fair's whole total came to 4 times that figure. The total was shared equally among 4 local charities. One of those charities is run by Carlos, who raised far less than Nina did at his own stall, and it later received a 56 dollar gift and then a 42 dollar gift. The fair also sold 310 hot dogs. How many dollars does Carlos's charity have from all of this?

A grain store began the month with 174 sacks of oats. 160 sacks were sent to a bakery, and another 10 went to a riding stable. Each sack that remained holds 7 kilograms of oats, and the store emptied them all into one bin. A farmer then poured 34 more kilograms into the same bin. The store weighs everything in kilograms even though its old scale is marked in pounds, and a dozen empty sacks are stacked by the door. How many kilograms of oats are in the bin?
